# h1: Fix: booking an appointment returns 500

It is 08:40 and the morning clinic opens at 09:00. Since Monday's deploy the front desk of the Hospital OPD cannot book an appointment: the booking request fails with a server error and the desk is writing patients on paper.

You are the Backend engineer on call. The app is finished and its tests are in the repo; something that changed on Monday broke it. Find out what, fix it in the files your role owns, and submit your work: Q runs every test, the Reviewer reads your change, and the Integrator merges it.

The team is in #incident-opd. Ananya (QA) has the report, Aarav (lead) wants updates, Karan owns the database layer. Ask them when you need to; every question you ask is counted.

## What to do
- tests/api/test_booking.py::test_booking_an_appointment_returns_201 passes
- tests/api/test_booking.py::test_editing_an_appointment_moves_its_time passes
- tests/api/test_booking.py::test_doctor_slots_list_the_booked_times_of_the_day passes
- add a regression test in `tests/regression/` (a file named `test_regression_<what>.py`) that fails on the code as it is now and passes after your fix
- the whole test suite passes: `python -m pytest -q`

## Files you may edit
- `backend/**`
- `tests/regression/**`

Do not edit these (they belong to the preset or to QA): `backend/main.py`, `backend/__init__.py`, `backend/api/__init__.py`, `database/__init__.py`, `database/connection.py`, `backend/validation.py`, `backend/seed.py`, `seed.json`, `static/ui-kit.css`, `static/ui-kit.js`, `static/shell.css`, `static/shell.js`, `static/fonts/**`, the generated tests in `tests/api`, `tests/ui` and `tests/qa`, and `.q/`.

## Acceptance tests
- `tests/api/test_booking.py::test_booking_an_appointment_returns_201`
- `tests/api/test_booking.py::test_editing_an_appointment_moves_its_time`
- `tests/api/test_booking.py::test_doctor_slots_list_the_booked_times_of_the_day`

The whole test suite in your folder has to pass: `python -m pytest -q`.

## Depends on
- nothing

## Where to work
- Folder: `C:\CODING\Hackathon\q\workspace\opd-bookings-down-14\.worktrees\backend`
- Branch: `agent/backend`
- Edit the files there with your own editor. Do not commit: Q does it when you submit.

## How to submit
Press **Submit** next to the task in Q's task list. Q runs the tests in your folder. If one fails, the task stays open and you see which. When they all pass, the Reviewer reads your change; at most 2 reviews can send it back with items to fix, and the next green submit is accepted. Then the Integrator merges it into the project and the tasks that waited for yours start.

"""Route stubs generated from the API contract. Fill in the bodies; keep paths, models and status codes."""
import json
import operator
import re
from typing import Literal
from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel
from backend.validation import Email, Phone, Positive, PositiveInt, Required, between
from database import appointments as db
from database import doctors as doctors_db

router = APIRouter()

class GetDoctorsAppointmentsByDoctor_idResponse(BaseModel):
    items: list

@router.get("/api/doctors/{doctor_id}/appointments", response_model=GetDoctorsAppointmentsByDoctor_idResponse)
def handle_get_doctors_appointments_by_doctor_id(doctor_id: int):
    # List the appointments of one doctor
    # error: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Doctor not found")
    # body: if doctors_db.get_doctor(doctor_id) is None: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Doctor not found")
    # body: return {"items": db.list_appointments(doctor_id=doctor_id)}
    if doctors_db.get_doctor(doctor_id) is None: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Doctor not found")
    return {"items": db.list_appointments(doctor_id=doctor_id)}

class PostDoctorsAppointmentsByDoctor_idRequest(BaseModel):
    patient_name: Required
    patient_phone: Phone
    date: str
    time: Required
    reason: str
    status: Literal['Booked', 'Completed', 'Cancelled']

class PostDoctorsAppointmentsByDoctor_idResponse(BaseModel):
    id: int
    doctor_id: int
    patient_name: str
    patient_phone: str
    date: str
    time: str
    reason: str
    status: Literal['Booked', 'Completed', 'Cancelled']
    created_at: str

@router.post("/api/doctors/{doctor_id}/appointments", status_code=201, response_model=PostDoctorsAppointmentsByDoctor_idResponse)
def handle_post_doctors_appointments_by_doctor_id(doctor_id: int, req: PostDoctorsAppointmentsByDoctor_idRequest):
    # Add a appointment to a doctor
    # error: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Doctor not found")
    # body: if doctors_db.get_doctor(doctor_id) is None: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Doctor not found")
    # body: return db.add_appointment(doctor_id=doctor_id, patient_name=req.patient_name, patient_phone=req.patient_phone, date=req.date, slot_time=req.time, reason=req.reason, status=req.status)
    if doctors_db.get_doctor(doctor_id) is None: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Doctor not found")
    return db.add_appointment(doctor_id=doctor_id, patient_name=req.patient_name, patient_phone=req.patient_phone, date=req.date, slot_time=req.time, reason=req.reason, status=req.status)

class PutAppointmentsByIdRequest(BaseModel):
    patient_name: Required
    patient_phone: Phone
    date: str
    time: Required
    reason: str
    status: Literal['Booked', 'Completed', 'Cancelled']

class PutAppointmentsByIdResponse(BaseModel):
    id: int
    doctor_id: int
    patient_name: str
    patient_phone: str
    date: str
    time: str
    reason: str
    status: Literal['Booked', 'Completed', 'Cancelled']
    created_at: str

@router.put("/api/appointments/{id}", response_model=PutAppointmentsByIdResponse)
def handle_put_appointments_by_id(id: int, req: PutAppointmentsByIdRequest):
    # Edit one appointment Answers 409 when: That status change is not allowed (the database refuses it by itself and the app turns that into the 409: never check it in the route function).
    # error: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Appointment not found")
    # body: row = db.update_appointment(appointment_id=id, patient_name=req.patient_name, patient_phone=req.patient_phone, date=req.date, slot_time=req.time, reason=req.reason, status=req.status)
    # body: if row is None: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Appointment not found")
    # body: return row
    row = db.update_appointment(appointment_id=id, patient_name=req.patient_name, patient_phone=req.patient_phone, date=req.date, slot_time=req.time, reason=req.reason, status=req.status)
    if row is None: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Appointment not found")
    return row

class DeleteAppointmentsByIdResponse(BaseModel):
    deleted: bool

@router.delete("/api/appointments/{id}", response_model=DeleteAppointmentsByIdResponse)
def handle_delete_appointments_by_id(id: int):
    # Delete one appointment
    # error: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Appointment not found")
    # body: if not db.delete_appointment(appointment_id=id): raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Appointment not found")
    # body: return {"deleted": True}
    if not db.delete_appointment(appointment_id=id): raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Appointment not found")
    return {"deleted": True}

class PostAppointmentsCompleteByIdResponse(BaseModel):
    id: int
    doctor_id: int
    patient_name: str
    patient_phone: str
    date: str
    time: str
    reason: str
    status: Literal['Booked', 'Completed', 'Cancelled']
    created_at: str

@router.post("/api/appointments/{id}/complete", response_model=PostAppointmentsCompleteByIdResponse)
def handle_post_appointments_complete_by_id(id: int):
    # Complete one appointment: sets status to Completed and return the updated appointment Answers 409 when: That status change is not allowed (the database refuses it by itself and the app turns that into the 409: never check it in the route function).
    # error: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Appointment not found")
    # body: row = db.complete_appointment(id)
    # body: if row is None: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Appointment not found")
    # body: return row
    row = db.complete_appointment(id)
    if row is None: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Appointment not found")
    return row

class PostAppointmentsCancelByIdResponse(BaseModel):
    id: int
    doctor_id: int
    patient_name: str
    patient_phone: str
    date: str
    time: str
    reason: str
    status: Literal['Booked', 'Completed', 'Cancelled']
    created_at: str

@router.post("/api/appointments/{id}/cancel", response_model=PostAppointmentsCancelByIdResponse)
def handle_post_appointments_cancel_by_id(id: int):
    # Cancel one appointment: sets status to Cancelled and return the updated appointment Answers 409 when: That status change is not allowed (the database refuses it by itself and the app turns that into the 409: never check it in the route function).
    # error: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Appointment not found")
    # body: row = db.cancel_appointment(id)
    # body: if row is None: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Appointment not found")
    # body: return row
    row = db.cancel_appointment(id)
    if row is None: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Appointment not found")
    return row

steps.title: Reproduce it
steps.text: Press Run tests and read which tests fail and the first error line of each. That is your starting point. Post a first update in #incident-opd within 2 minutes, and answer Aarav within a minute when he asks.

steps.title: Open the failing route
steps.text: The error names a function and a file under backend/api/. Open backend/api/appointments.py and find the call that fails.

steps.title: Find what changed
steps.text: Something changed on Monday. The database/migrations folder is read-only for you but you can read it: open the newest migration.

steps.title: Tell the team
steps.text: Post what you found in #incident-opd (Agent Chat tab). Aarav is waiting for an update; you can also ask Karan or Ananya.

steps.title: Add a regression test
steps.text: Add a regression test in tests/regression/ that fails before your fix. Name the file test_regression_<what>.py and copy the style of tests/api/test_booking.py. Run it: it has to be red now and green once the code follows the database.

steps.title: Fix it in your files
steps.text: Change the files you own so that every caller says what the database layer says now. The same name is used in two files under backend/api/.

steps.title: Run the tests again
steps.text: Run tests. The whole suite has to be green, not only the three acceptance tests.

steps.title: Submit for review
steps.text: Press Submit for review. The Reviewer reads your change and may send it back up to twice.
